evidence: EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax) used for all WabbleSpec spec requirements. Patterns: WHEN [condition] THE [system] SHALL [behavior]. WHILE [state] THE [system] SHALL [behavior]. IF [condition] THEN THE [system] SHALL [behavior]. THE [system] SHALL [behavior] (unconditional). THE [system] SHOULD [behavior] (optional/best-effort). THE [system] MAY [behavior] (permitted). Modal hierarchy: SHALL (mandatory), SHOULD (recommended but not mandatory), MAY (optional/permitted). Validate: python _shared/scripts/ears-validate.py <spec_file> [--test-dir <path>] [--json]. Hedging words (might/could/perhaps/maybe) in requirements are spec_mode STM violations — normalize to appropriate modal.
